**My Mission: Verifying Hardware Component Presence in the VHL Project Library**

As the Librarian Agent, my primary objective is to meticulously verify that all non-trivial hardware components essential for the current circuit design are indeed present within the VHL project library. This is a critical step to ensure a complete and functional design before proceeding.

My systematic approach is as follows:

Firstly, I will **read the SCUD (System Component Usage Definition)** file, which is located at `/tmp/vhl_e2e_workspace_vdgn55_c/bms-project_e2fe16b5_bms-monitor-module/bms-monitor-module/bms-monitor-module.scud`. This document serves as the foundational source of truth for the design's component requirements.

Next, I will **extract the list of components** from the "Components Inventory" section of the SCUD. It's important to note that I will be focusing on genuine hardware components and will deliberately **ignore any built-in elements** that are inherent to the system or simulation environment and don't represent discrete physical parts.

Following that, I will **inspect the current project library**. This involves navigating to `/tmp/vhl_e2e_workspace_vdgn55_c/bms-project_e2fe16b5_bms-monitor-module/bms-monitor-module/Workspace/imports` to ascertain which components have already been successfully imported or added. This will provide me with a baseline of what's currently available.

The core of my task then becomes **resolving any missing components**. For every non-trivial component identified in the SCUD but absent from the project library, I will leverage the `tsci search` command to locate its availability and then utilize `tsci import/add` to bring it into the project scope. This ensures that every required piece of hardware is accounted for.

Finally, once all components have been verified and any missing ones have been acquired, I will **update the SCUD file** by appending a "Library Mapping" section. This section will clearly document the association between the components defined in the SCUD and their corresponding library representations, creating a comprehensive record for future reference and maintenance.

With this plan in place, my immediate next step is to begin by reading the SCUD file itself.
